variables.claim_asserts: Perissodactyla are phylogenetically closer to Leporidae than to other ungulates, and Leporidae are closer to Perissodactyla than to other rodents.
variables.test_measures: Most-recent-common-ancestor clade membership for representative perissodactyl, leporid, artiodactyl, and rodent tips in the Open Tree synthetic mammal phylogeny, checked against NCBI named clades.

modality.note: Phylogenetic tree topology is the direct modality for comparative claims about closer evolutionary relationship.

assumptions.note: Reading 'more closely related' as more recent common ancestry matches the historical-inference conclusion; multiple representative tips avoid relying on one species per group.

scope.claim_scope: Phylogenetic relationships among Perissodactyla, Leporidae, other ungulates, and rodents.
scope.test_scope: Three perissodactyls, three leporids, three artiodactyls, five rodents, two other 1917 ungulates, one other lagomorph, and outgroups in the current synthetic mammal tree.

reasons: The smallest clade joining all perissodactyl and leporid tips contains all sampled artiodactyl and rodent tips, directly evaluating both asserted proximity comparisons.
The smaller perissodactyl-plus-artiodactyl clade has six tips and excludes Leporidae, while the leporid-plus-rodent clade has nine tips and excludes Perissodactyla.
NCBI taxonomy independently encodes Perissodactyla with Artiodactyla in Laurasiatheria and Leporidae with Rodentia in Glires, matching the tested topology.
The test does not measure Thompson's skull transformation, but the claim record asserts the phylogenetic inference, which tree topology directly addresses.
what_would_change_it: A species-level phylogenomic analysis showing a supported Perissodactyla-Leporidae clade excluding Artiodactyla and Rodentia would change the assessment of the tested relationship.
